## Project Structure

```
src/
  app/              # Next.js App Router pages
    (admin)/        # Admin panel (auth-gated)
    about/          # About page
    api/            # API routes
    [...slug]/      # Dynamic post/category pages
  components/       # Shared UI components
  lib/              # Core utilities (data, auth, config, smtp)
  modules/          # Feature modules (posts, categories, events, banners, rss-feeds, users, public-users)
  shared/           # Cross-cutting concerns (cache, database, locks, middleware, utils)
  queue/            # In-memory job queue
  workers/          # RSS worker
  proxy.ts          # Next.js proxy/middleware: /post/* 410 handling, X-Robots-Tag on article paths (matcher skips every path starting with `sitemap`)
  lib/sitemaps.ts   # Split sitemaps (log #766): shared queries + XML for the route handlers below
  app/sitemap_index.xml, app/sitemap.xml   # Sitemap index (both URLs serve the same index)
  app/sitemap-news.xml     # Google News sitemap: last 48h, excludes press-release
  app/sitemap-posts/[page] # Served as /sitemap-posts-N.xml via next.config rewrite; 1000 posts/file, oldest-first by id
  app/sitemap-events.xml, app/sitemap-static.xml   # Upcoming partnership events; static pages + 5 staff authors
cron/               # Cron job definitions (RSS feed scheduler)
scripts/            # DB migrations, seed, import, export, backfill scripts
public/             # Static assets (no default next/vercel starter SVGs)
docs/               # Documentation (this agent lives here conceptually)
```

## About Us Page (`/about-us`)

- **Route:** `/about-us` (distinct from the older `/about` above — this is the canonical one)
- **Files:** `src/app/about-us/page.tsx` (client component, pink/cream editorial-magazine layout: hero, stat panel, video-card row + dot carousel, 6-icon pillar grid, "What We Do" CTA, footer bar), `src/app/about-us/layout.tsx`
- **Isolated Tailwind v4 build, fully automatic, one shared CSS file for both isolated-Tailwind routes (interaction #419)** — no manual regeneration step, no per-route CSS file:
  - `src/app/isolated-tailwind.css` (one level up from this route, shared with `/advertise-with-us`) is both the Tailwind *source* (has `@import`/`@theme` directives for **both** routes) AND the exact file `layout.tsx` imports (`import "../isolated-tailwind.css"`). There is no separate compiled-output file and no CLI command to remember — `@tailwindcss/postcss` (enabled project-wide in `postcss.config.mjs`) compiles it automatically as part of Next's normal webpack CSS pipeline, on every `npm run dev` and `npm run build`, exactly like a standard Tailwind project. Just edit `page.tsx` classNames and run the normal build/dev command. Webpack correctly dedupes the shared import into a single compiled chunk served to both routes (confirmed: one ~13KB chunk containing both `au-*` and `adv-*` utilities, not two separate ones).
  - `postcss.config.mjs` has `@tailwindcss/postcss` listed **before** `postcss-import` (order matters — `postcss-import` doesn't understand Tailwind's `@import "tailwindcss/theme.css" source(none)` syntax and will mis-resolve it as a plain file import if it runs first; this was the actual cause of the old "Module not found" errors that originally justified the manual-CLI workaround). Verified this doesn't affect `globals.css`/`style.css`/`media-queries.css` at all — `@tailwindcss/postcss` only transforms files that actually contain Tailwind directives; everything else passes through byte-for-byte unchanged (confirmed via identical compiled-output hash before/after, both when this was first set up in #418 and again after merging into one shared file in #419).
  - `isolated-tailwind.css` still needs `source(none)` on both `@import`s + one explicit `@source` line **per route** (`./about-us/page.tsx` and `./advertise-with-us/page.tsx`, relative to the shared file's own location) — remove any of these and Tailwind falls back to scanning the whole repo for candidate classes, which once picked up bracket-syntax example text in this very `agent.md` and generated broken CSS that crashed the build (interaction #410). If a third route ever wants to join this shared Tailwind setup, add another `@source` line there rather than creating a new file.
  - **Cascade-layer gotcha (root-caused in interaction #412) still applies:** the `@import` lines must **not** use `layer(theme)`/`layer(utilities)` — that would wrap the output in named `@layer` blocks, which lose every cascade battle against the site's unlayered legacy reset. Keep the imports plain.
  - Still runs under PM2 in **production mode** (`next start`): after any `page.tsx` className change, just `npm run build` (no separate CSS-compile step anymore) then `pm2 restart dev-startupgpt`.
- **Reference source of truth:** a hand-designed static `about-us (1).html` prototype the owner approved — theme tokens (`--color-au-pink`, `--color-au-pink-deep`, `--color-au-ink`, `--color-au-muted`, `--color-au-line`, `--color-au-bg`, `--color-au-panel`, `--color-au-fade`) live in `isolated-tailwind.css`'s `@theme` block, named after that prototype's CSS custom properties.

## Submit Your Funding Round Page (`/submit-funding-round`)

- **Route:** `/submit-funding-round` — public lead-gen page, **front-end only: no backend/DB write**, same as Feature Your Startup and Submit Your Press Release. Completely redesigned 2026-09-08 (log #687) from a gradient-hero "fanned card stepper" wizard into a cinematic, deep-charcoal editorial scrolling experience, per an explicit design brief the user provided (premium VC-platform/luxury-editorial tone, serif display typography, monochrome palette with the site's pink used only sparingly, one continuous scroll rather than a click-gated form).
- **This redesign uses the exact same 7-field `useLeadForm("funding-round")` data model as before** (`name`, `companyName`, `phone`, `email`, `website`, `countryCity`, `pdfFile`) — **no new backend/validation fields were invented**, even though the brief's own template chapter list assumed richer fields (Funding Amount, Currency, Round, Lead/Other Investors, structured "Story" fields, separate Logo/Founder Image uploads) that this app's backend has never had. The brief itself said not to invent backend fields, so the 5 template chapters were consolidated into what the 7 real fields actually support — see the chapter list below. The one PDF upload (`pdfFile`) is still where round size/stage/investors/use-of-funds/story all go, exactly as before the redesign.
- **Files:** `src/app/submit-funding-round/page.tsx` (route + metadata, untouched), `src/components/funding-round-submit/` — `FundingRoundPage.tsx` (orchestrator: owns the `useLeadForm` controller, a scroll-spy `IntersectionObserver` for the sticky rail, and `handleSubmit`, which validates all 6 non-derived fields at once via the same validator functions from `lead-forms/shared/validation.ts` and jumps to the first invalid chapter rather than gating step-by-step), `FundingHero.tsx` (cinematic line-by-line serif headline reveal + an abstract CSS/SVG "growth" visual — ascending bars, thin orbit rings, a ghost "26" numeral — deliberately not a stock photo), `FundingMilestone.tsx` (editorial "Every funding round tells a story" transition, asymmetric 2-col), `FundingProgressRail.tsx` (sticky vertical chapter nav on desktop / sticky horizontal bar on mobile, purely presentational), `ChapterHeader.tsx` + `ChapterContinue.tsx` (shared chapter chrome), `chapters/{ChapterCompanyFounder,ChapterContact,ChapterMaterials,ChapterReview}.tsx`, `SubmissionSuccess.tsx` (self-drawing ring+checkmark confirmation, replaces the whole chapters/rail section once `ctrl.submitted`), `FundingTrust.tsx` (4-reason monochrome trust grid, content carried over from the old `WhySubmit.tsx`), `FundingClosing.tsx` (final CTA before the site's global footer), `motion.ts` (shared Motion variants/easing), `chapters.ts` (the 4-chapter id/label metadata), `icons.tsx` (gained `ArrowRightIcon`/`ArrowDownIcon`; `RocketIcon`/`LockIcon` are now unused but left in place, harmless).

- **The 4 chapters** (`chapters.ts`): **01 Company & Founder** (Company Name, Your Name, Phone/WhatsApp — canonical fields `companyName`/`name`/`phone`), **02 Contact & Presence** (Official Email, Website optional, Country/City optional — `email`/`website`/`countryCity`), **03 Supporting Materials** (the funding deck PDF upload, max 10MB — `pdfFile`), **04 Review** (editorial `<dl>` summary of every field with per-row "Edit" links back to the owning chapter, plus the real Submit button). All 4 chapters are mounted simultaneously (not hidden behind Next/Back) — the reader can scroll and fill fields in any order; the sticky rail's active-chapter highlight is driven by a live (not fire-once) `IntersectionObserver`, separate from each chapter's own one-time `whileInView` entrance reveal.

This required no changes to the shared hook itself (`src/components/lead-forms/shared/useLeadForm.ts`, still the same `stepGroups`-generalized version from log #685) — Feature Your Startup and Submit Your Press Release are completely unaffected by this page's redesign.

- **Not verified live in-browser for this round of changes** — `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` are both clean, and a thorough manual cross-check confirmed every class used in the new TSX files has a matching CSS rule (one intentional harmless exception, `fr-upload-field`, which was already always-unstyled-but-harmless on every sibling lead-gen page too), all `FormField`/chapter DOM ids are unique now that every chapter is mounted simultaneously, and a real bug was caught and fixed by re-reading the code rather than a screenshot: the scroll-spy `IntersectionObserver` was originally set up in a `useEffect` with `[]` deps, so after `ctrl.submit()` unmounts the chapters (replaced by `SubmissionSuccess`) and "Submit Another Round" (`ctrl.reset()`) remounts fresh ones, the observer would have kept watching the detached original DOM nodes forever — fixed by keying the effect on `ctrl.submitted` so it re-attaches to the new elements each time the chapters remount. **Why no live check happened**: while restarting throwaway dev servers to verify this page, broad `lsof -ti:<port-range> | xargs kill` port-freeing commands accidentally killed this box's real pm2-managed production processes (`startupgpt-dev` and `morningpulse`) multiple times each — both auto-restarted by pm2 and came back `online` with no apparent lasting damage, but this was disclosed to the user immediately and they chose to skip live verification and check it in their own environment instead, rather than risk further process/port interference. **Standing rule for any future session touching this box**: never run a port-range kill sweep — port 3000 (and evidently others) are live pm2 processes, not spare dev-server leftovers; use a specific known-free port the user confirms, the same way log #656/#660's throwaway `next dev` sessions used port 3099 specifically.

## Tailwind CSS Migration Status

### Styling Rule Going Forward

- **Final target: Tailwind-only codebase, including removal of existing CSS.**
- Do **not** add new custom CSS, CSS Modules, `<style jsx>`, or static inline `style={{}}` props.
- Use Tailwind utilities, arbitrary values, responsive variants, `group`/`peer` states, and `tailwind.config.js` extensions for animations/design tokens.
- Treat all remaining custom/legacy CSS as migration debt to remove, not as a permanent dependency.
- When replacing existing CSS, migrate the behavior into TSX Tailwind classes instead of creating new stylesheet rules.
- Existing CSS may remain only temporarily during incremental migration to avoid breaking pages.
- **(log #456)** Old/legacy code is not proactively rewritten to Tailwind on its own — only convert a file when it's already being touched for a real feature/fix, matching how every "✅ Done" row above actually happened (as part of other work, not a dedicated sweep). New development always uses Tailwind from the start.

**ALL CONTROLLABLE SURFACES USE TAILWIND IN TSX — LEGACY THEME CSS STILL LOADED (interaction #46 clarified)**
Public pages, public components, and admin UI are authored with **Tailwind utility classes** wherever we control the markup. The project **still loads legacy theme CSS** (`styles/style.css`, `styles/media-queries.css`) plus `globals.css` overrides because the homepage and article layouts depend on **`mvp-*`** and related theme classes until a full redesign replaces that layer. **`@tailwind base` is intentionally not used** — it breaks the theme float/sticky layout (see interaction #9). **Exceptions:** TipTap admin editor (`<style>` injections for editor chrome + pasted content), 410 HTML in `proxy.ts`, Font Awesome CDN `@import` in `globals.css`.

## Database & Migrations

- Migration SQL files in `scripts/migrations/`
- Key tables: posts, banners, rss_feeds, events, users, categories
- Notable fields: `post_robots`, `meta_description`, `scheduled` status, `gone_410`, `event_end_date_time`
- `partnership_events.social_instagram / social_linkedin / social_x / social_facebook` (VARCHAR(500) NULL, log #791) — organiser's optional social links from `/list-your-event` step 4. **Create-only**: `PartnershipEventsRepository.create()` writes them via `CREATE_ONLY_COLUMNS`, `update()` never does; admin `POST /api/admin/partnership-events` and CSV `importEvents` strip them. Shown read-only in the Partnership Tracker Edit modal (section 11) and in the Excel export. Shared list + validation: `SOCIAL_LINK_FIELDS` / `normalizeSocialLink` / `socialLinkError` in `modules/partnership-events/domain/types.ts`. Migration `add-partnership-events-social-links.sql` — **applied on dev 2026-09-14 (log #794)**, not yet on live.

### Schema Change Workflow (formalized log #456 — was already the de-facto practice, now a hard rule)

- **Never run ad-hoc SQL directly with no file behind it.** Any DB schema change (new table, new column, altered constraint) must be written as a real `.sql` file in `scripts/migrations/` first, then applied — the file is what lets the same change be replayed on production later, since this checkout's database is the **live dev DB** (see [[deploy_pm2_gotcha]] — `dev.startupgpt.fyi` served live via PM2 from this checkout), not production itself.
- Naming follows the existing convention: `add-<feature>-<table-or-column>.sql` (e.g. `add-hr-payroll-leave-days.sql`).
- Running a migration against the live dev DB requires user confirmation first (established pattern throughout the Interaction Log).
- Log entries for schema-changing work note "Not yet deployed" until the user confirms the same `.sql` file has been run against the actual production database — dev being migrated is not the same as prod being migrated.

- Entry: `cron/index.ts`
- Run once: `npm run cron:rss-feeds`
- Persistent: `npm run cron:start`

## Admin Panel

- Located at `src/app/(admin)/`
- Auth: `src/lib/admin-auth.ts` (JWT-based)
- Admin data hook: `src/hooks/useAdminData.ts`

### Admin Sidebar Menu Items
Dashboard, Posts, Events, Event Regions, Categories, Authors, Banners, RSS Feeds, **Registered Users** (`/admin/registered-users`)
(List above predates several later additions — see `src/components/admin/AdminSidebar.tsx` `menuItems` for the current full set, which also includes Partnership Tracker, Newsletter, **Sales Report**, Tools, Reports, Brand Stories, Database/Contacts, Users.)

### Sales Tracker (`/admin/sales-tracker`, renamed from Sales Report, see log #392) — DB-backed since log #409
- A standalone leads/CRM tracker (Add/Edit lead, screenshot/voice-note AI extraction, team members, filterable table, status/type breakdown + bar charts), embedded via `<iframe src="/api/admin-tools/sales-tracker/index.html">` in `src/app/(admin)/admin/sales-tracker/page.tsx`, served by `src/app/api/admin-tools/[tool]/[file]/route.ts` (whitelisted tool/file lookup — see `AdminIframeTool.tsx`).
- Source lives in `src/modules/admin-tools/sales-tracker/` (`index.html` + `styles.css` + `script.js`), not `public/` (moved at some point after the original 2026-08-08 add) — kept out of the app's own CSS/component tree by design, per the original user request.
- **Persistence (log #409):** was `localStorage`-only (not shared across team members, despite the tool's own "Shared across your team" subtitle) — migrated to real MySQL tables `sales_leads` + `sales_team_members` (`scripts/migrations/add-sales-tracker-tables.sql`). Backend: `src/modules/sales-tracker/` (domain/repository/service) + `src/app/api/admin/sales-tracker/{leads,leads/[id],team}/route.ts`, gated by `SALES_TRACKER_ROLES` (`admin` only, `src/shared/middleware/roles.ts`). Frontend `script.js` now calls these routes directly (`apiGetLeads`/`apiSaveLead`/`apiDeleteLead`/`apiDeleteAllLeads`/`apiGetTeam`/`apiAddTeamMember`/`apiRemoveTeamMember`) instead of `storageGet`/`storageSet`; all hardcoded `sampleLeads()`/`sampleTeam()` dummy data removed, table starts empty until real leads are entered.

### HR Tool ("Huey", `/admin/hr-tool`, display label "HR Management" per log #408) — DB-backed since log #409
- A full standalone HR system prototype (directory, onboarding e-sign flow, attendance/punch, leave, expenses, payroll, tickets/helpdesk, compliance calendar, letter templates, Rules & Org Structure, audit log) with its own internal role-play login (Employee ID, any password) layered on top of — and independent from — the site's real admin auth. Embedded the same way as Sales Tracker: `src/app/(admin)/admin/hr-tool/page.tsx` → `/api/admin-tools/hr-tool/index.html` → `src/modules/admin-tools/hr-tool/script.js` (~1960 lines, single `state` object driving synchronous re-renders).
- **Persistence (log #409):** previously **zero persistence** — a hardcoded `state` seed that reset on every page reload, explicitly commented `"In-memory data store (no backend — resets on reload)"`. Migrated to 19 real MySQL tables (`hr_teams`, `hr_designations`, `hr_expense_categories`, `hr_required_documents`, `hr_holidays`, `hr_employees`, `hr_onboarding`, `hr_attendance`, `hr_attendance_overrides`, `hr_punch_log`, `hr_regularizations`, `hr_leave_requests`, `hr_expenses`, `hr_tickets`, `hr_compliance_tasks`, `hr_payroll_runs`, `hr_templates`, `hr_rules` singleton, `hr_audit_log`) — see `scripts/migrations/add-hr-tool-tables.sql`.
- Backend: `src/modules/hr-tool/` (domain/types.ts covers every entity; `repository/hr-tool.repository.ts` + `repository/shared.ts`'s generic `replaceAllRows`/`findAllRows` helpers; `service/hr-tool.service.ts`) + `src/app/api/admin/hr-tool/*` routes (one `GET /bootstrap` that returns the whole initial state in one call, `PUT` bulk-replace routes for list entities, `POST` upsert routes for single-record entities like attendance/punch/payroll-runs/audit-log/templates/[name]), gated by `HR_TOOL_ROLES` (`admin` only).
- Frontend rewiring pattern: `state` starts as an empty skeleton, `loadAll()` fetches `/bootstrap` at boot before first render; every mutating function became `async` and now `await`s a matching `persist*()` helper (defined near the top of `script.js`) right after mutating local `state`, before re-rendering — e.g. `persistEmployees()` does `PUT /employees` with the full `state.employees` array. `logRuleChange()` (audit log) is fire-and-forget (`persistAuditEntry`, not awaited) since it's called from ~15 non-critical sites.
- **Dummy data removed, real setup kept:** all demo employees/onboarding/attendance/leave/expense/ticket records removed. Org structure (teams, designations, expense categories, required documents, holidays), letter templates (Offer Letter / Employment Agreement keep their real DOTFYI Media Ventures boilerplate; other 5 template types seeded empty), and policy `rules` defaults were kept as seed data — the tool's own `resetSampleData()` button already drew this exact line ("kept Teams, Org Structure, Rules, and Templates, since that's real setup, not sample data"). **One employee is seeded** (`E-105`, Divya Menon, HR Head) so there's a way to log in at all post-migration — team `manager` fields pointing at now-removed demo employees were nulled out.
- **Note (log #426):** the two paragraphs above describe the original iframe/`script.js` build; the tool was since rewritten to native React (`src/app/(admin)/admin/hr-tool/page.tsx` → `HrToolProvider`/`HrToolApp` in `src/components/admin/hr-tool/`, backed by the same `src/modules/hr-tool/` API) — this section hasn't been fully rewritten to match yet, treat file paths above as historical. As of log #426: the internal "Huey" Employee ID + password login screen (`views/Login.tsx`) is bypassed — opening HR Management always lands directly on the `Founder` HR-role (`HrToolContext.tsx`'s `resolveFounder()`), since the outer route is already `admin`-only. A new **Assigning IDs** People-tab (`views/AssigningIds.tsx`, Founder-only) lets the Founder issue a real Employee ID + password (bcrypt-verified, stored in the new `hr_employee_credentials` table — see `src/modules/hr-credentials/`) and optionally link it to an existing Publisher Admin / Event Admin `panel_admins` account, at which point that account's original email/password login is retired in favour of Employee ID + password (`PanelAdminsService.loginWithEmployeeId`, `/admin/login`'s new Email/Employee ID tab toggle). Full detail in log #426.
- **Note (log #429):** Publisher Admin/Event Admin now have their own Punch In/Punch Out card directly on their `/admin` dashboard (`src/components/admin/AttendanceWidget.tsx`), gated by a new route group `src/app/api/admin/attendance/` (`requireAnyRole(['event_admin','publisher_admin'])` — separate from `HR_TOOL_ROLES`). It resolves their identity via `HrCredentialsService.getByLinkedPanelAdminId()` (reverse lookup off the JWT's `panel_admins.id`) and writes into the same `hr_attendance`/`hr_punch_log` tables described above, so their punches show up directly in the Founder's Attendance view (`views/Attendance.tsx`, now also showing Employee ID + Role columns via `HrBootstrap.employeeCredentials`). Once-per-day is enforced server-side (calendar-day reset), unlike the original Employee self-service flow which only checked this client-side. Full detail in log #429.
- **Note (log #439):** DB audit found all 19 `add-hr-tool-tables.sql` tables present and seeded in live `zox_db`, but `hr_employee_credentials` (the `add-hr-employee-credentials-table.sql` migration underpinning Assigning IDs / employee login since log #426) had never actually been run — the code referencing it (`hr-credentials` module, `panel-admins` repository, `employee-auth` middleware) would have failed at query time. Migration run against live `zox_db`; table now exists (empty, 0 rows).

- **Note (log #445):** `AttendanceWidget.tsx` (the shared Punch In/Out card on both the Publisher/Event Admin and plain-employee dashboards) is no longer a "punch buttons + last 14 days" list — it's now a selected-date table (Date/Status/Punch In/Punch Out, with the punch buttons living inside the table and only appearing when the selected day is today) paired with a big navigable month calendar whose day cells are color-coded green/orange/red by how that day's punch-in landed against the admin's shift start + grace period. This required adding real per-day lateness data that didn't exist before: `hr_attendance.in_minutes` (new column, `add-hr-attendance-in-minutes.sql`) — previously only `hr_punch_log` (single row per employee, overwritten daily) had the raw punch-in minutes, so past days had no way to answer "how late were they that day." `/api/admin/attendance/me` and `/api/employee/attendance/me` now take `?month=YYYY-MM` and return that month's day-by-day records (`calendar`) instead of a flat recent-history list.
- **Note (log #446):** Employees can now request attendance regularization themselves (previously only the Founder's own internal whole-array-replace flow existed, which an isolated employee/Publisher/Event Admin session could never safely call). From `AttendanceWidget.tsx`, selecting a date with a late/grace-period punch-in shows an "Apply for Regularization" button (reason required, capped by a new admin-set monthly quota, blocked once a request already exists for that date); submitted dates render light blue on the calendar regardless of approval outcome. New `hr_rules` columns: `regularizationMonthlyQuota`, `shortLeaveMaxHours`, `shortLeaveMonthlyQuota` (all editable in Rules & Org Structure). Employees never see the exact grace-period minute value anywhere in the Attendance module (admin-set, deliberately hidden so it can't be gamed) — but they DO see it, along with every other policy number, on the new dedicated **Rules & Policy** page (`PolicySummaryWidget.tsx`, sidebar entry on both dashboards) — that page is the intentional policy-transparency surface; the day-to-day Attendance calendar is not. `HrToolService.getShiftSettings()` no longer exists — superseded by `getPolicySummary()`.
- **Note (log #450):** Payroll (`views/Payroll.tsx`) is no longer fake. It used to be `ctc/12` minus a hardcoded flat 7.8% with zero attendance/leave awareness and nothing ever actually stored — "Run Payroll" just flipped a status flag. Now `HrToolService.computePayrollForMonth()`/`runPayroll()` compute real Net Pay = Monthly Gross − (LOP days × Gross÷30), where an LOP day is a working day (not Sunday, not a Holiday-calendar date) with no punch and no approved leave — persisted per-employee-per-month in the new `hr_payroll_entries` table once "Run Payroll" is clicked (frozen; re-clicking recomputes and overwrites). No deductions (PF/ESI/TDS) in this V1 — deliberately deferred, not silently approximated. `HrPayrollRun.month` changed from a human label ("August 2026") to a canonical `YYYY-MM` key — anything reading `state.payrollRun.month` for display needs `monthKeyToLabel()` from `components/admin/hr-tool/utils.tsx`. **Superseded by log #453 below** — the ÷30 rate and month-based cycle described here have both changed.
- **Note (log #451) — important, read before touching Payroll/Directory again:** `hr_employees` (CTC, DOJ, status — used by Payroll and Directory) and `hr_employee_credentials` (Assigning IDs — the actual live hiring flow, has no CTC field, is what attendance is keyed against) are two independent tables that don't auto-sync. The old Onboarding→e-signature pipeline that used to create `hr_employees` rows is dead (unreachable since log #426). Payroll now sources *who appears* from `hr_employee_credentials` (via a `PayrollRosterEntry[]` built in the API `_lib.ts`, not inside `HrToolService`, to keep it decoupled from hr-credentials per its own documented rule), enriching with `hr_employees` data by name-match when it exists; an employee with no `hr_employees` row still shows with `ctc: 0` and a "Set salary" button in Payroll's admin table rather than disappearing. Setting a salary there creates the `hr_employees` row if none exists yet (same defaults as Directory's CSV import). Also split `HrPayrollEntry.presentDays` (was conflating "actually punched in" and "on approved leave" into one number) into separate `presentDays` and `leaveDays` — new `hr_payroll_entries.leave_days` column. **Superseded by log #452 below** — Directory's identical blind spot (flagged here as a known gap) is now fixed.
- **Note (log #452):** Assigning IDs is gone as a separate section — merged into Employee Directory, with hiring now a single flow. `Directory.tsx`'s "+ Send offer letter" (now `HireEmployeeButton.tsx`, replacing the old `DraftOfferLetterButton.tsx`) collects name/designation/team/email/CTC (offer letter fields) AND Employee ID/password/photo/panel-role-link (Assigning IDs fields) in one form — no field asked twice — and on approval creates BOTH the `hr_employee_credentials` login AND the `hr_employees` Directory record together (with the merged offer letter text saved directly on `signedDocs`), employee active immediately (no more fake "awaiting e-signature" limbo, since that stage was never reachable anyway — confirmed dead code, `views/Login.tsx`, deleted nowhere but still orphaned/unused). `hr_employees` gained a real link column, `credential_id` (nullable, soft reference — no FK, since `hr_employees` is saved via whole-table delete/reinsert which a constraint would fight); old rows (Divya Menon, and anyone from before this change) keep `credential_id = NULL` and fall back to name-matching exactly as before, no behavior change for legacy data. New `CredentialFields.tsx` holds the shared Employee-ID/password/panel-role form markup + validation (`nextEmployeeCode`, `generatePassword`, `validateCredentialFields`), reused by both the new hire flow and a new `EditCredentialModal.tsx` — the latter opened from Directory's employee profile (Founder-only, stricter than the rest of the profile modal which HR Head can also see, matching Assigning IDs' original Founder-only gate) for password resets/photo/panel-role changes on an already-hired employee, or to retroactively issue a login for an employee who never had one (e.g. old CSV imports). Full file list: added `HireEmployeeButton.tsx`, `CredentialFields.tsx`, `EditCredentialModal.tsx`; deleted `AssigningIds.tsx`, `DraftOfferLetterButton.tsx`; `'assigning-ids'` removed from `HrView`/`VIEW_ACCESS`/`NAV_GROUPS`/`VIEWS`. Deliberately out of scope (confirmed with user before building): reviving Onboarding.tsx's document-upload/e-signature checklist pipeline — that machinery is fully built and already wired, just still has no reachable path feeding it real records; a natural, separate follow-up. Went through full Plan Mode (research → Plan agent → user confirmation on the one real scope question) given the size and sensitivity (creates real login credentials). Hit and fixed a genuine `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint quirk while extracting the panel-admin-lookup effect into `CredentialFields.tsx`: the rule only recognizes the "cancellation-token subscription" exception when the effect's called function takes *only* the `{cancelled}` signal object as its argument — passing other reactive values alongside it (even if the signal is also present) makes it fall back to a flat "no sync setState in effects" violation. Fixed by having the loader function close over the reactive values instead of receiving them as params, matching `Payroll.tsx`'s already-clean `loadPayroll(signal)` shape exactly. `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on every touched file. Migration run against live `zox_db` with user confirmation. Not yet tested live.
- **Note (log #454):** The hire form's button label in Employee Directory is "+ Add Employee" now (was "+ Send offer letter" — that label stayed as-is in Onboarding.tsx's own copy of the same button, since the ask was Directory-specific). `CredentialFields.tsx` gained two opt-in props to support this: `showAvatar` (default true; `HireEmployeeButton` passes `false` — no photo field at hire time, still available later via `EditCredentialModal`, which doesn't pass the prop so keeps its default) and `idRowExtra` (a slot next to the Employee ID field for whatever the caller needs in that same row — `HireEmployeeButton` uses it for Date of Joining, so those two now sit side by side instead of DOJ having its own separate row above).
- **Note (log #458) — regularization now splits by punch type (in vs. out):** Previously one `hr_regularizations` row per date, punch-in only. `hr_regularizations` gained `punch_type` (`'in'|'out'`, default `'in'`) and `requested_time` (the specific time the employee is asking be recorded) via `add-hr-regularizations-punch-type.sql` — one date can now carry up to two rows, submitted independently. `HrRegularization` gained `punchType`/`requestedTime`; repository's `findRegularizationByEmpAndDate` renamed `findRegularizationByEmpDateAndType` (now scoped by type too, so 'in' and 'out' don't collide); a shared `mapRegularizationRow()` replaced the three duplicated row-mapping literals. `HrToolService.submitEmployeeRegularization(emp, date, reason, punchType, requestedTime)` branches eligibility by type: punch-in unchanged (must be late/grace-period); punch-out is newly eligible whenever that date's punch-out is missing (the existing "Forgot to punch out" reason option had no mechanism behind it before this). Both employee-facing self-service surfaces (`AttendanceWidget.tsx` — plain employees and Publisher/Event Admin; the Founder's own `views/Attendance.tsx` submit modal; and the Founder's per-day `AttendanceCalendar.tsx` modal, a third, independent self-service submission path that had the same single-row assumption) now show two separate buttons/actions — "Regularize Punch In" / "Regularize Punch Out" — each opening its own reason + time form, so a date with both regularized shows two distinct entries. Admin approval tables (`views/Attendance.tsx`'s regularization list, `AttendanceCalendar.tsx`'s day-detail modal) gained Type/Requested Time columns — approval itself is still just a status change, doesn't auto-write the requested time back into `hr_attendance`/`hr_punch_log`. Confirmed pre-existing: the Founder's HR Management → Attendance page already lets HR Head/Founder approve/reject any employee's regularization (`ApprovalCell`) and already lists every submitted request there (`scopedApprovals` returns the full list for admin roles) — no change was needed for that part, since employee submissions and Founder review already share the one `hr_regularizations` table. `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on every touched file. Migration run against live `zox_db`. Not yet tested live.
- **Note (log #453) — the live payroll cycle is now 26th–25th, keyed by end month:** `hr_rules.salary_period_from/to = 26/'25'` (was 1/'last'). A cycle like "26 Jul–25 Aug" is stored/displayed under the key `"2026-08"` (the month it *ends* in — matches conventional payroll labeling) — `payrollPeriodRange(monthKey, rules)` in `src/modules/hr-tool/utils/time.ts` resolves that key backward into the actual date range. Whenever "the current cycle" needs resolving client-side, use the new `currentPayrollMonthKey(rules)` from that same file — **not** the old `currentMonthKey()` (still exists in `components/admin/hr-tool/utils.tsx` but is calendar-month-only and will pick the wrong cycle near the wrap boundary). "Run Payroll" now unlocks 5 days before the cycle's real end date (`PayrollPreview.canRun`/`runUnlocksAt`), not after it "ends" — days that haven't happened yet when run early are simply not counted at all (not wrongly treated as LOP). "Present" requires punch in AND out. LOP's per-day rate is ÷ the cycle's actual day count, not a fixed ÷30.
- **Note (log #515) — "Remove employee" is now a real cascade delete:** it used to save the shortened employee list through `PUT /api/admin/hr-tool/employees` (whole-table replace of `hr_employees` only), so the employee's `hr_employee_credentials` row survived — and `Directory.tsx`'s orphan auto-heal effect (log #452) immediately recreated the Directory record from that surviving Employee ID, making the delete look like it silently did nothing. Removal now goes through a dedicated `DELETE /api/admin/hr-tool/employees/[id]` → `HrToolService.deleteEmployee` → `HrToolRepository.deleteEmployeeCascade`, which in one transaction deletes the employee row, their Employee ID credential (matched `credential_id` first, `name` second — the same resolution Directory uses, and needed because pre-#452 rows have `credential_id = NULL`), their `hr_onboarding` row, and every `emp`-keyed row in `hr_attendance`, `hr_attendance_overrides`, `hr_punch_log`, `hr_regularizations`, `hr_leave_requests`, `hr_expenses`, `hr_tickets`, `hr_payroll_entries`, plus nulls any `hr_teams.manager` / `hr_employees.manager` pointing at their name. Client side, `HrToolContext.deleteEmployee(employee)` prunes exactly the same things from state (including `employeeCredentials`, so auto-heal has nothing left to resurrect) and throws on failure so Directory can alert with the server's real message instead of the usual silent save-failed warning. Deleting the credential also kills any live employee-portal session immediately — `requireEmployeeAuth` re-reads the credential per request. "Mark as exited" is unchanged and remains the correct action for a real exit.
- **Note (log #493):** Founder's Attendance → Regularization requests table no longer needs horizontal scrolling to read the Reason column — see `HrToolApp.tsx`'s new `.wrap-table` modifier class and `Attendance.tsx`'s `<colgroup>` on that one table.
- **Note (log #777) — Geo-fenced punching (server-enforced):** the Rules-page **Geo-fencing** toggle (`hr_rules.geo_fencing`) was dead UI; it now gates a real check. When on, Punch In **and** Punch Out are accepted only if the browser's GPS fix is within `hr_rules.geo_fence_radius_m` (default **50 m**) of the office point `hr_rules.geo_fence_lat/lng` (seeded to the StartupNews.fyi office, Jhandewalan: **28.644533, 77.2003635**; Founder-editable under the toggle, radius clamped 10–500 m, lat/lng inputs never fall back to 0,0). Rule (`src/modules/hr-tool/utils/geofence.ts`, pure haversine): no reading → `GEOFENCE_LOCATION_REQUIRED`; reported accuracy > 100 m → `GEOFENCE_IMPRECISE`; distance > radius + min(accuracy, 50 m) → `GEOFENCE_OUTSIDE`. `HrToolService.punchEmployee(emp, type, location?)` does the check (duplicate-punch check first, then geofence; when the toggle is off the location is ignored and not stored). All three punch routes — `/api/admin/attendance/punch`, `/api/employee/attendance/punch`, and the new `/api/admin/hr-tool/punch` (HR_TOOL_ROLES, replaces the Founder view's client-side raw `/punch-log` upsert and its fake "Geolocation captured." alert) — accept `{ type, location?: {lat,lng,accuracy} }` and return **403 + `code`** for GEOFENCE_* refusals (409 `ALREADY_PUNCHED` unchanged). Per-punch audit stored on both `hr_punch_log` and `hr_attendance`: `in_lat/in_lng/in_accuracy_m/in_distance_m` and `out_*` (`HrPunchGeo` on `HrPunch.inGeo/outGeo`, `HrAttendanceRecord.inGeo/outGeo`, all optional/nullable; `decideRegularization` carries them through so an approval doesn't NULL them). Client: shared `src/lib/browser-geolocation.ts` (`getCurrentBrowserLocation()` — checks `window.isSecureContext` first, high-accuracy, 15 s timeout, `maximumAge: 0`; `geofenceHintFor(code)`), used by `AttendanceWidget.tsx` (reads `geofence: {enabled, radiusM}` from `/me`, button shows "Getting your location…") and the Founder's `views/Attendance.tsx` (`hrApi.punch` → `applyServerPunch` local-state mirror in `HrToolContext`). `getPolicySummary()` now also exposes `geoFencing`/`geoFenceRadiusM` (not lat/lng), and `PolicySummaryWidget.tsx` shows a "Punch location — Within R m of office" row when on. Migration **`scripts/migrations/add-hr-geofence.sql`** — **applied to live `zox_db` on 2026-09-13 (log #778)**; verified `hr_rules` row = geo_fencing 0 / 28.6445330 / 77.2003635 / 50 and all 8 audit columns present on both tables. Note there is **no `mysql` client binary on this box** — SQL migrations are applied with a small `tsx` script that uses the project's own `getDbConnection()` pool (`@next/env` for `.env`), run with `NODE_PATH=<project>/node_modules` if the script lives outside the repo. Geolocation needs HTTPS or localhost (`dev.startupgpt.fyi` is HTTPS; `http://<ip>:3000` on a phone will never work).

### Public User Registration System
- **DB table:** `public_registrations` (auto-created on first API call via `ensureTable()`)
- **Module:** `src/modules/public-users/` (domain/types.ts + repository/public-users.repository.ts)
- **API routes:** `POST /api/public-auth/register`, `POST /api/public-auth/login`, `POST /api/public-auth/google-verify`
- **Admin API:** `GET /api/admin/registered-users` (requireAdmin, paginated)
- **Frontend:** `src/components/AuthModal.tsx` — bottom slide-up auth banner + floating pill; included in `layout.tsx`
- **Auto-popup behavior:** Logged-out users get an auth banner that slides up from the bottom after scrolling about 900px unless dismissed recently; dismiss applies a 10-minute cooldown instead of suppressing the popup for the entire tab session.
- **Auth storage:** `localStorage` keys `pub_auth_token` + `pub_auth_user`
- **JWT:** `{ pubUserId, email, type: 'public' }`, 30-day expiry, same `JWT_SECRET` as admin
- **Google Sign-In:** GIS library, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` env var (currently empty — uses fallback button)
- **Protected nav:** REPORTS link (`requiresAuth: true` in config) fires `open-auth-modal` event if not logged in

## Team & Workflow

- **Tony** — Team Lead / Senior Dev. Assigns work and gives final approval/go-ahead.
- **Jarvis** (this agent) — middle layer both ways: receives task requests from Tony and passes them down to Happy; then receives Happy's completed work, does QC (code quality review + testing/typecheck), and reports back up to Tony for approval.
- **Happy** — Junior Dev. Receives tasks (via Jarvis) and implements them.

**Request flow (downward):** Tony asks Jarvis → Jarvis passes the task to Happy.
**Delivery flow (upward):** Happy implements → Jarvis QC's (code quality review + testing/typecheck) → Tony approves → go ahead.

## PWA (Progressive Web App) — added 2026-08-21

- **Manifest:** `src/app/manifest.ts` (Next.js file convention → served at `/manifest.webmanifest`). `name`/`short_name` "StartupNews.fyi"/"StartupNews", `start_url`/`scope` `/`, `display: standalone`, `theme_color` `#E72262` (brand pink), icons at `public/icons/icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `icon-512-maskable.png` (maskable version has the mark scaled to ~62% on a solid brand-color canvas so OS mask shapes never clip it — regenerated from `src/app/icon.png` via PIL). Includes `related_applications: [{ platform: "webapp", url: "<site>/manifest.webmanifest" }]` for `getInstalledRelatedApps()` self-detection; `prefer_related_applications` intentionally left unset.
- **Service worker:** `public/sw.js` — has a real `fetch` handler (required alongside the manifest for Chromium to ever fire `beforeinstallprompt`). Navigations: network-first → cached copy → `/offline.html`. `/_next/static/*`: cache-first. Icons/manifest/logo: stale-while-revalidate. Everything else: network only, never cached. Explicitly bypasses `/api/*`, `/admin*`, `/dashboard*`, `/employee*` so a stale cache can never shadow authenticated content. `skipWaiting`/`clients.claim`, purges old cache versions on `activate`, accepts a `SKIP_WAITING` postMessage.
- **Offline fallback:** `public/offline.html` — standalone/self-styled, no framework dependency.
- **Registration:** `src/components/ServiceWorkerRegister.tsx` (mounted once in `src/app/layout.tsx`) registers `/sw.js` on window `load` in production only; in dev it actively unregisters any leftover worker so it can't serve stale dev chunks.
- **Install popup:** `src/components/InstallPWA.tsx`, mounted in `layout.tsx` **before** `<AuthModal />` (DOM order matters here — see stacking-context note below), bottom-center fixed card (`z-index: 9999`), modes `install`/`ios`/`installed`/`none`.
  - **Stacking-context gotcha (found 2026-08-21):** `#mvp-site-main` (`globals.css`) sets `z-index: 9999` *and* `backface-visibility: hidden` — the latter forces that element to establish its own stacking context, which means the entire page-content subtree (everything `ConditionalLayout` renders — header, articles, footer, all of it) stacks as one unit at 9999, regardless of any individual descendant's own `z-index: auto`. An earlier attempt at 9998 for this card lost to that unit every time, on every page, which is why the card rendered correctly in the DOM (right `display`/`visibility`/`opacity`, right coordinates) but was still visually painted over — confirmed by an automated `elementFromPoint()` check at the card's own screen coordinates returning a `.mvp-feat1-feat-text` element from deep inside the homepage hero, not the card. Fix: match `#mvp-site-main`'s 9999 exactly and rely on document order for the tie-break (later-in-DOM wins ties at equal z-index) — `InstallPWA` mounts after `ConditionalLayout` closes, so it wins against `#mvp-site-main`; `AuthModal` mounts after `InstallPWA` (also at 9999, its bottom-sheet z-index), so it in turn wins against the install card, preserving "behind the auth modal." Any *new* body-level fixed overlay in this codebase needs to either clear 9999 or accept losing to page content — 9000-ish, which looks "high enough" by the numbers, is not. Visual style: horizontal toast layout (brand-color icon tile on the left, title+subtitle in the middle, primary action + a plain-text secondary link stacked on the right, thin brand-color top border) matching a reference screenshot the user supplied. Chromium: listens for `beforeinstallprompt`, stores the event, `Install` button calls `.prompt()` (once only). iOS Safari (incl. iPadOS, detected via `platform === "MacIntel" && maxTouchPoints > 1`): manual Share → Add to Home Screen instructions, since that platform never fires the Chromium event. "Already installed" detection ladder: standalone/`navigator.standalone` check (writes a sticky `pwa_installed_at` localStorage marker) → that marker on a later visit → `getInstalledRelatedApps()` (Chromium-only, feature-detected) → a "Chromium-silence probe" (if `beforeinstallprompt` hasn't fired ~3s after `navigator.serviceWorker.ready`, conclude installed — doesn't write the sticky marker itself, and a later `beforeinstallprompt` always overrides it back to `install` mode and clears any marker). Synchronous parts of this ladder run in a lazy `useState` initializer (not an effect) because this repo's ESLint config enforces `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` — confirmed by lint failing on the first draft before this rework.
- **Sequencing behind the auth modal:** `AuthModal.tsx` dispatches a `window` `CustomEvent('auth-modal-state', { detail: { open } })` whenever any part of its flow (bottom sheet or the post-signup welcome overlay) is visible, edge-triggered so `open:false` only ever fires after an `open:true` did. `InstallPWA` gates all rendering on an `authBusy` flag from that event, armed ~10s after the flow closes (per the user's explicit request — the task brief's original number here was ~900ms, revised up), ~3s after load for already-signed-in visitors (checked via `pub_auth_token` + re-checked on the existing `pub-auth-changed` event), or a ~10s solo fallback if nothing else armed it.
- **Dismissal:** two separate 14-day localStorage keys (`pwa_install_dismissed_at`, `pwa_hint_dismissed_at`) via helpers in `src/lib/pwa-storage.ts`, all routed through try/catch (private-browsing throws). Declining the native Chromium install dialog also sets the install key.
- **Live status:** deployed via `./deploy.sh` on 2026-08-21 (see interaction log #469) — `/manifest.webmanifest`, `/sw.js`, `/offline.html`, and the install card are confirmed live on `dev-startupgpt`.

## System Atlas — auto-generated architecture + DB reference (added 2026-08-29)

- **What it is:** `docs/SYSTEM_ATLAS.html` — a standalone, self-contained HTML reference covering system architecture, the full API/frontend route surface, three data-flow diagrams (auth across all four login paths, a cached-read request lifecycle, the RSS ingestion pipeline), the five background cron jobs, and the complete MariaDB schema (53 tables across 6 domains: Content, Users & Auth, HR Tool, Sales & Partnerships, RSS & Newsletter, Misc), each table rendered as a collapsible column-reference card plus a per-domain Mermaid ER diagram. Renders its Mermaid diagrams via CDN `mermaid.js` (needs internet on first open per browser, then cached) — no build step, just open the file directly.
- **How it stays current:** `.git/hooks/post-commit` (local to this machine, not tracked by git — `.git/hooks` is never committed) watches every commit for changes under `src/modules/`, `src/app/api/`, `src/shared/{database,cache,middleware,locks}/`, `scripts/init-db.sql`, `scripts/migrations/`, `cron/`, `src/queue/`, `src/workers/`. On a match it runs Jarvis headlessly in the background (`claude -p ... --dangerously-skip-permissions`, binary at `~/.npm-global/bin/claude` — installed there, not `/usr/lib/node_modules`, because the system npm prefix wasn't writable by this user) to re-derive the doc from current source and rewrite `docs/SYSTEM_ATLAS.html` in place, preserving its existing design. It does **not** auto-commit — the regenerated file is left in the working tree for review, and the run logs to `.git/system-atlas-update.log`. Because that headless run executes inside this repo, it inherits this same `CLAUDE.md` and is bound by the same Jarvis mandate below (interaction-log entry + `agent.md` knowledge update) as any other change made here.
- **Known limitation:** this hook is per-machine (lives outside version control), so it doesn't follow the repo to a fresh clone or another developer's machine without being reinstalled the same way.
- **Note on `CLAUDE.md`'s stated Project Root:** it names `/home/tech/Startupsnews-NewNextJS-main`, which doesn't exist in this environment — the actual working repo is `/home/ubuntu/zox-nextjs`, and this `agent.md` lives there. Treating the actual repo location as authoritative rather than the stale path.

## Reports System

- **Feature scope:** Admin-managed reports library with public member-facing access in the dashboard.
- **Admin routes:** `/admin/reports`, `/admin/reports/create`, `/admin/reports/edit/[id]`
- **Public member route:** `/dashboard/reports`
- **Admin APIs:** `src/app/api/admin/reports/route.ts`, `src/app/api/admin/reports/[id]/route.ts`
- **Public API:** `src/app/api/reports/route.ts`
- **Repository:** `src/modules/reports/repository/reports.repository.ts`

### Reports Data Model

- **Table:** `reports`
- **Columns:** `id`, `title`, `description`, `file_url`, `thumbnail_url`, `file_name`, `file_size`, `mime_type`, `is_active`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
- **Index:** `idx_reports_active_created (is_active, created_at)`
- **Storage:** report files and thumbnails are stored in S3 and referenced by URL.

### Reports Repository Behavior

- `ReportsRepository.ensureTable()` creates the `reports` table if missing.
- The repository also self-heals older production schemas by auto-adding missing columns and the active/created index.
- `file_size` values are normalized to plain numbers before JSON responses to avoid MariaDB `BIGINT` serialization failures.
- Public report listing uses `findActive()` so only active reports are exposed to members.

### Admin Reports Notes

- Admin reports pages use shared admin auth helpers and token fallback handling because some environments strip `Authorization` headers.
- Report upload flow supports direct file upload with S3 presigned URLs.
- Manual fields for file name, file size, and MIME type were removed from admin forms because they are derived automatically from the uploaded file.

### Dashboard Reports Behavior

- `src/app/dashboard/reports/page.tsx` fetches reports dynamically from `/api/reports` using the public auth token from `src/lib/public-auth.ts`.
- The current member page is intentionally simplified compared with earlier iterations.
- Removed from the page UI: summary counters, tag/category pill filters, preview badge overlay on thumbnails, format/pages metadata card, and the remaining reports count text under the search box.
- Current page keeps: hero section, search, report cards, and preview modal.
- The current report cards use a large top thumbnail, oversized editorial title styling, a compact pages/date row, and a bordered right-aligned CTA while still opening the existing preview modal.
- The card proportions were later tightened with a smaller desktop grid, slightly shorter media sizing, and reduced title/meta/button scale for a more compact presentation.
- The cards were then reduced again with a narrower desktop min width, tighter internal spacing, and smaller title/meta/button sizing for an even more compact layout.
- On large screens, the reports grid now uses a fixed four-column layout so four cards can sit in a single row instead of relying on auto-fill behavior.
- Report thumbnails now use contained image rendering inside the media box so the full uploaded image stays visible instead of being cropped.
- Thumbnail boxes now use a soft gradient backdrop derived from each report's color palette so contained images blend into the card more naturally.
- The thumbnail backdrop was later refined into a stronger layered gradient finish with a soft radial highlight so the image area feels more polished and color-led.
- Report card clicks no longer open the old preview modal; they now check `pub_auth_token` and route authenticated users into the dashboard flow while sending unauthenticated users to the public login prompt.

### Current Preview Behavior

- Report cards use `thumbnail_url` as the visual cover when available.
- Opening a report preview uses the uploaded document `file_url` inside a modal when available.
- The preview modal was refined for desktop and mobile sizing so the document uses the available space more cleanly.
- Direct download actions were removed from the member dashboard UI.
- Browser-native PDF toolbar suppression is limited because the preview currently uses the raw document URL in an iframe.

### Operational Notes

- If reports fail with 500s, likely causes previously seen in production were:
  - missing `reports` table columns/index on older schema
  - MariaDB `BIGINT` JSON serialization from `file_size`
  - stripped admin auth headers on admin report pages
- If uploads fail from the browser, S3 bucket CORS must allow the application origin.

### Dashboard Overview Notes

- The old `/dashboard` overview page was removed as the landing surface.
- `/dashboard` now redirects directly to `/dashboard/reports`.
- The earlier dedicated `/api/dashboard/stats` endpoint remains in the codebase, but the dashboard root no longer renders the old overview UI.

### Dashboard Shell Notes

- The shared dashboard sidebar was simplified to a cleaner shell with just the logo, user identity, primary nav items, and logout action.
- The old membership card, secondary nav descriptions, and back-to-site footer action were removed from the sidebar.
- The collapsed desktop rail and mobile drawer were both narrowed so the sidebar behaves better on smaller screens and no longer wastes as much horizontal space.
- In the collapsed desktop state, the brand area now shows only the logo block instead of the full title text.
- The expanded sidebar header was also simplified so the top brand area shows only the logo block, without the StartupNews title text.
- The shared nav was updated so reports is now the primary dashboard destination instead of the removed overview page.

### Dashboard Settings Notes

- `/dashboard/settings` was simplified to remove the extra stat cards, membership benefits, notification preferences, profile tips, quick actions, and danger zone panels.
- The current settings page keeps the profile edit form as the primary surface, with a smaller account snapshot sidebar.
- The profile form area no longer shows the old read-only member/account/status strip, and the copy was updated to avoid membership wording on that page.

### Agent Note

- From this point onward, new project knowledge should be appended at the end of `agent.md` in sections like this, in addition to adding rows to the Interaction Log.

(4) Design/maintenance: the entire repository, cron job, and `BRAND_STORIES_ROLES` constant are hand-duplicated from Reports with no shared abstraction — future fixes need manual re-application to both. | 381 | 2026-07-30 | Follow-up: user said the report **preview modal** itself ("preview") was still slow — different from the grid-load issue fixed in #380. Root-caused two compounding issues specific to `/dashboard/reports`' PDF preview (`src/app/dashboard/reports/page.tsx`): (1) **S3 CORS was hiding range-request support from pdf.js.** Verified via direct `curl -H "Range: bytes=0-1023"` against the S3 object that the bucket (`$S3_BUCKET`, `us-east-1`) *does* support byte-range requests (`Accept-Ranges: bytes`, `206 Partial Content`), but `aws s3api get-bucket-cors` showed the bucket's CORS `ExposeHeaders` only allowed `ETag` through to browser JS — `Accept-Ranges`/`Content-Range` aren't CORS-safelisted response headers, so pdf.js running in the browser couldn't detect streaming support and fell back to downloading the entire PDF (one live report is 13.2MB) before rendering page 1. Fixed by `aws s3api put-bucket-cors`, adding `Accept-Ranges`, `Content-Range`, `Content-Length` to `ExposeHeaders` (kept `AllowedOrigins`/`AllowedMethods`/everything else identical — purely additive) — user explicitly approved this live-infrastructure change first. Verified after: the same range `curl` now shows `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: ETag, Accept-Ranges, Content-Range, Content-Length`. (2) **The viewer rendered every PDF page at once** regardless of scroll position — `Array.from({ length: pdfNumPages })` mounted a full-resolution `<Page>` for all pages immediately on document load. Changed to incremental rendering: new `pdfVisiblePages` state (starts at 2, reset alongside `pdfNumPages` on report change) caps how many `<Page>`s are mounted; a callback-ref-attached `IntersectionObserver` (`pdfSentinelRef`, `rootMargin: '600px 0px'`, rooted on the existing `pdfViewportRef` scroll container) on a 1px sentinel div after the last rendered page bumps `pdfVisiblePages` by 2 as the user scrolls near the bottom, so a 10-page report only pays full-res canvas rendering cost for pages actually being viewed. Rebuilt (`npm run build`) and restarted (`pm2 restart dev-startupgpt`) with user's prior approval from #380 covering the same deploy step; re-verified both the app (200s) and the S3 range/CORS behavior live afterward. `tsc --noEmit` clean. |

Per the CSS Cascade Layers spec, unlayered rules always beat layered ones regardless of specificity or source order, so every single about-us Tailwind utility — borders, padding, margins, grid gaps — was silently losing to the legacy reset even though it was correctly present in the served CSS bundle, which is exactly why #411's classes-exist check passed while the page still looked broken. Fix: removed `layer(...)` from both `@import` lines so the CLI emits unlayered output that wins via normal specificity instead (the input file's own header comment already *described* this as deliberate — the actual `@import` lines just contradicted it). There is no `middleware.ts` at the project root (only unrelated per-request auth helpers under `src/shared/middleware/`, used inside API routes, not Next.js Edge Middleware) — so `/admin` and `/admin/login` are publicly reachable, plain 200 HTML at the HTTP level. Auth is enforced entirely client-side inside `src/app/(admin)/layout.tsx`'s `checkAuth()`, which only runs after JS/hydration. `public/robots.txt` disallows `/admin` and `(admin)/layout.tsx` sets `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">`, but both only ask well-behaved crawlers not to *index* the page — neither blocks access nor has any effect on GA, which tracks purely from client JS execution regardless of robots.txt. Net effect: any real browser hit on those URLs — genuine staff logging in (explains the long engagement time) or bots/scanners probing for an admin panel (a near-universal, constant background occurrence on any public site) — gets counted as a session landing there. (2) **`(not set)` landing page** — the same `gtag.js`/`gtag-init` `<Script>` tags use `strategy="lazyOnload"`, which Next.js defers until the browser is idle, i.e. after the page has already rendered and, in an App Router site with client-side navigation, potentially after the URL has already changed. If a session's first hit fires late enough to miss a clean `page_location` (fast bounce, bot/prerenderer that doesn't stick around for the idle callback, or a quick client-side redirect like `AdminLayout`'s `router.replace('/admin/login')` for unauthenticated `/admin` visits), GA4 can't populate the landing-page dimension and reports `(not set)`; the accompanying 0 new users on those 76 sessions is consistent with bot/bounce traffic rather than real visitors. No code changes made — diagnosis only, per user's request. |

| 453 | 2026-08-18 | **Payroll V2** — a set of real calculation fixes to the V1 engine (#450/#451), all confirmed with the user via `AskUserQuestion` first since this is real-money math. **(1) Payroll cycle is now 26th–25th, not 1st–last day**: `payrollPeriodRange()` rewritten so `monthKey` names the cycle by the month it *ends* in (e.g. "26 Jul–25 Aug" = key `"2026-08"`, the chosen convention — most payroll systems label by payout month) rather than the month it starts in; the wrap-around now goes *backward* into the previous month instead of forward into the next. `hr_rules` singleton row updated live (`salary_period_from=26, salary_period_to='25'`) plus both `DEFAULT_RULES` copies, so this is the actual configured cycle now, not just a supported option. **(2) "Current cycle" resolution had to become period-aware**: the old `currentMonthKey()` (just `today`'s calendar month) would pick the wrong cycle for several days each month once cycles could span two calendar months — added `currentPayrollMonthKey(rules)` to `time.ts` (finds which cycle, by end-month key, today actually falls inside) and switched `Payroll.tsx` and `HrToolContext.tsx`'s initial `payrollRun.month` to use it. **(3) "Run Payroll" unlocks 5 days before the cycle's actual end** (not month-end, and not "must have fully ended") — new `RUN_PAYROLL_UNLOCK_DAYS_BEFORE_END` constant, `runUnlocksAt`/`canRun` added to `PayrollPreview`/`PayrollApiResult`. Running early is now a real, intended use — so days that haven't happened yet (`date > evalTo`, where `evalTo = min(periodEnd, today)`) are simply not judged present/leave/LOP at all rather than wrongly counting as LOP for not having occurred yet; Working Days still always reflects the *full* period regardless of when it's run, since that's a calendar fact, not a time-based one. Re-running after the cycle actually ends (already-supported recompute-and-overwrite) picks up the remaining days for real. **(4) "Present" now requires a full punch — in AND out**, not just a punch-in (previously a punch-in alone counted as present all day). **(5) Per-day LOP rate switched from a fixed ÷30 to ÷ the cycle's actual day count** (`periodDays = eachDateInRange(clippedFrom, to).length`), since 26th–25th cycles run 29-31 days depending on the month; confirmed this is mathematically equivalent to the user's own description of the formula ("present + leave + holiday days, added up, gives the salary") — `Gross − LOP×(Gross/periodDays) ≡ Gross × (paidDays/periodDays)` algebraically, just computed the more numerically-direct way. **(6) Real display bug fixed**: `AttendanceCalendar.tsx` (Payroll's own calendar, Founder view + My Payslips self-view — confirmed in scope, the employee dashboard's separate `AttendanceWidget.tsx` calendar was confirmed out of scope) had zero awareness of Sundays or the Holiday calendar at all — a day with no punch record just showed as generic "Not recorded" (or, if a punch record happened to exist for that date for any reason, whatever raw status it carried, misleadingly implying "present"). Added an explicit Sunday/holiday check (`isSunday()` + `state.orgStructure.holidays`) that now always renders as "Week-off" — taking priority over any punch data — unless an HR manual override says otherwise; fixed both the calendar cell coloring and the day-detail modal's status label, which had the same blind spot independently. **(7) DOJ (date of joining) added as a required field on the "Send Offer Letter" hire form** (`HireEmployeeButton.tsx`) — previously hardcoded to "today," which broke the mid-cycle-join clipping logic for anyone whose actual start date differed from when their offer was processed; kept `signedDate` (when the letter was generated) separate from `doj` (when they actually start) — different concepts, both real. Working Days' Sunday/holiday exclusion in `computePayrollForMonth` itself needed no change — it was already correct (confirmed by hand against the user's own worked example: 31-day cycle, 5 Sundays + 2 holidays → 24 working days), the bug was specifically in the calendar *display*, not the payroll *calculation*. `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on every touched file. `hr_rules` data update run against live `zox_db` with user confirmation. Not yet tested live. |

Root cause: `#mvp-site-main` (`globals.css`) sets `z-index: 9999` *and* `backface-visibility: hidden` — the latter triggers a stacking context on that element, so the whole page-content subtree it wraps stacks as one 9999-level unit regardless of any descendant's own `z-index: auto`. The card's z-index at the time (9998, from #469) always lost to that unit, on every page — this is why it "looked over 9000" by the numbers but was still visually buried; full write-up now in the "PWA" section's new stacking-context-gotcha bullet. Fix: `InstallPWA`'s z-index changed 9998 → 9999 (exact match), and its mount order in `layout.tsx` swapped to *before* `<AuthModal />` (was after) so document-order tie-breaking still resolves correctly both ways — the card now wins its tie against `#mvp-site-main` (mounts later in the DOM) while `AuthModal` (mounts later still) continues to win its tie against the card, preserving "behind the auth modal" without needing a z-index value that doesn't exist (nothing sits strictly between 9999 and `AuthModal`'s welcome-overlay peak of 10000). Verified the fix *before* touching the shared `.next`/PM2 process this time, having learned from #469's incident: `rsync`'d the working tree (minus `node_modules`/`.next`/`.git`) into a scratch dir, symlinked the real `node_modules` in to skip a full reinstall, ran a fully isolated `npm run build` there, served it via `next start -p 3001` in the background, and re-ran the `elementFromPoint()` check plus a new one that dispatches `open-auth-modal` and confirms the auth sheet (also z-index 9999) still paints on top of the install card and the card correctly disappears while `authBusy` is true — both passed — before killing the port-3001 process and deploying the real change to `dev-startupgpt` via `./deploy.sh` as before. Post-deploy: all key routes 200, PM2 restart counts stable, no crash-loop. |

Fixed by moving it to a real native `addEventListener('wheel', ..., { passive: false })` in a `useEffect`, which actually allows `preventDefault()`. Also swapped the `window.resize`-only layout tracking for a `ResizeObserver` on the track element (catches layout shifts a window resize wouldn't, e.g. web-font-swap reflow). Verified all of this live post-deploy via headless Chromium: simulated a wheel gesture over the carousel and confirmed the *carousel* scrolled (404px) while the *page* `scrollY` stayed at 0 (proof the passive-listener fix works), zero console warnings/errors, and a fresh screenshot confirming the 3-per-row layout from #484 is still intact. `tsc --noEmit`/`eslint` clean. | 522 | 2026-08-27 | **High-priority bug on the public `/submit-event` wizard: picking a Country never registered** — the dropdown opened and listed countries, but selecting one left the field empty (and the preview card stuck on "International"). Not a CSS/dropdown problem at all — `CustomSelect` was working correctly. Root cause was a **stale-snapshot React state write** in `useSubmitEventForm.ts`: `updateAndMaybeValidate()` wrote `const next = { ...data, [key]: value }; setData(next);` — a *value* update built from the render snapshot the handler closed over — while its siblings `setField`/`setFields` correctly used *functional* updates. React's queue applies a functional update to the accumulated state but lets a value update **replace state wholesale**, so `CountryCityFields`'s country `onChange`, which deliberately fires four setters in one tick (`onChangeCountry` → `onChangeCountryOther('')` → `onChangeCity(firstCity)` → `onChangeCityOther('')`), played out as: functional country write lands → snapshot write reverts everything to the pre-click render → functional city write lands on that reverted object → second snapshot write reverts again. Net result `{ ...data, cityOther: '' }`, i.e. **both the country and the auto-selected city were thrown away**. Grepped every call site first: `updateAndMaybeValidate` is used by ~15 handlers but the country dropdown is the only one firing multiple setters in a single tick, which is exactly why this reproduced there and nowhere else (the phone-code custom field calls it alone, ContactStep/DateVenueStep one field per change). Fixed by making the data write functional (`setData((prev) => ({ ...prev, [key]: value }))`); since the validator could then no longer be handed a `next` snapshot, revalidation moved to a new `pendingRevalidation` ref + `useEffect` on `[data]` that recomputes queued error messages **after** the commit — which is strictly more correct than before, because the validator now sees every field a single handler changed rather than only its own (matters for `validateCountry`, which reads both `country` and `countryOther`). Bonus enabled by that: `EventBasicsStep`'s `onChangeCountry`/`onChangeCity` moved from bare `setField` to `updateAndMaybeValidate`, so a visible "Please select a country." now clears the instant one is picked instead of waiting for blur. Verified by replaying React's actual update-queue semantics in a standalone script (function update → applies to accumulator, value update → replaces): old sequence yields `country=''`/`city=''` from a pick of India/Ahmedabad, new sequence yields `country='India'`/`city='Ahmedabad'` — bug reproduced and fix confirmed. `tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint` clean across the whole `src/components/submit-event/` directory. **Note for future work in this hook: never reintroduce a snapshot-based `setData(obj)` — every write must be functional, since several handlers here legitimately fire more than one setter per tick.** Not built or deployed, per the standing hold — this one is a live public-form bug, so it needs a build + `pm2 restart dev-startupgpt` to actually reach users. |

| 537 | 2026-08-29 | User reported that Punch Out couldn't be clicked until Punch In had been clicked, and asked for the mechanism fixed so someone who forgets to punch in can still punch out. Traced every punch surface first rather than assuming which one they meant: the HR Tool's own `views/Attendance.tsx` was **already correct** (its Punch Out button is gated only on `punchedOutToday`, and `punchOut()` explicitly handles the no-punch-in case), and so was the **server** — `HrToolService.punchEmployee()` rejects only a duplicate punch of the same type and already sets `note = 'No punch-in recorded today.'` for an out with no in. The real gate was purely client-side in `AttendanceWidget.tsx` (the widget used by `/admin/attendance`, `/employee/attendance`, and the Publisher/Event Admin dashboard): the Punch Out cell rendered its button only when `(isSelectedToday && hasIn)`, so with no punch-in there was no button at all — not a disabled one. Fixed to `isSelectedToday`, which is all the server ever required. **Found and fixed a second, worse blocker that the user's exact scenario walks straight into:** having punched out with no punch-in, that employee could then never correct the day, because a missing punch-in has *no lateness bucket* (`latenessBucket(null, rules)` returns `null`) and both layers treated null as ineligible — the client's `canRequestInRegularization` required a non-null, non-'on-time' bucket, and `submitEmployeeRegularization()` rejected `bucket === null` with "Only a late punch-in (grace period or later) can be regularized." That inverted the feature's intent: a punch that never happened is precisely what regularization is for; only an *on-time* punch-in has nothing to correct. Both layers now reject only `'on-time'` (server error message reworded to "That punch-in was on time — there is nothing to regularize."), leaving the regularization window, the monthly quota, the duplicate-request check and RM/HR approval as the real bounds. Also dropped the client's `hasIn` requirement from `canRequestOutRegularization` (a day with neither punch could regularize neither — and the server's out branch only ever checked `hasOut`, so the client was stricter than the server for no reason), and **added future-date guards on both sides** (`isSelectedFuture` on the client, `if (date > todayStr())` on the server) — necessary because allowing a null bucket would otherwise have made every not-yet-arrived day in the current month look regularizable, and the server's window check uses `diffDays > windowDays`, which a negative diff passes. Net: Punch In and Punch Out are now independently clickable, punching out without punching in is recorded with the server's existing warning note, and the resulting gap can actually be regularized afterwards. `tsc --noEmit`/`eslint` clean on both touched files. Not built or deployed, per the standing hold. |

| 672 | 2026-09-08 | User asked what the "pre-existing error" I kept mentioning (#667-#671) actually was and to fix it. **Explained**: `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` fires when a `useEffect` calls `setState` synchronously as its first action (e.g. `setMounted(true)` in an empty-deps effect) — React renders once, the effect runs, and immediately triggers a second render just to flip that flag. Not a functional bug, but an avoidable extra render; the modern fix for exactly this "is this the client yet" flag is `useSyncExternalStore`, which reads the client/server difference directly instead of rendering twice. **Fixed**: added `src/hooks/useHasMounted.ts` (a `useSyncExternalStore`-based hook: `getServerSnapshot` returns `false`, `getClientSnapshot` returns `true`, `subscribe` is a no-op since there's nothing to actually subscribe to — this is a constant, not a changing value) and swapped it in for the `useState(false)` + `setMounted(true)`-in-effect pattern in both `DashboardHome.tsx` and `UserDashboardLayout.tsx`. Confirmed via `grep` that `setMounted` is now gone from both files entirely, and via a throwaway `next dev` (port 3099, stubbed auth + APIs) that the dashboard and sidebar still render and navigate identically. **Caveat surfaced, not fixed**: removing `setMounted` didn't reduce the total ESLint error count — in both files that same effect (and, in `UserDashboardLayout.tsx`, two *other* effects) turned out to have more than one synchronous `setState` call each; the linter only ever reports the first per effect, so fixing the first one just exposed the next: `setUser(...)` (reading the auth user from `localStorage`) in both files, plus `setReportsExpanded`/`setBrandStoriesExpanded` (syncing sidebar submenu state to the current pathname) and `setMobileOpen(false)` (resetting mobile-drawer state when the viewport leaves mobile width) in `UserDashboardLayout.tsx`. These are a different, legitimate category — actually synchronizing local state with an external system (localStorage, the current route, viewport width) rather than a constant client/server flag — with no equally clean one-line fix; resolving them would mean restructuring several effects for a non-functional, performance-style lint rule. Left as-is and reported this transparently rather than quietly declaring the error "fixed" while 4 near-identical ones remained under it. `tsc --noEmit` clean project-wide. The font-size formula (still divided by 24.63) now only controls how big the heading reads; it can no longer put the step out of alignment even if that number is off.
